messages.author: 9af7c0e584af0222
messages.subject: consensus map in Rqtl for NAM population
parts:
Dear Karl,
We have NAM population with 4 families. I want to construct a intergrated map for these four families. I have SNP data for four families. Can we do this in rqtl?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] consensus map in Rqtl for NAM population
parts:
For map construction, I think you could relabel the alleles in each family and treat them as a single family of RILs.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] consensus map in Rqtl for NAM population
parts:
I guess it depends on the nature of the NAM populations.

When I hear "NAM" I think of multiple panels of biparental recombinant inbred lines (RILs), where the parents are drawn from some population (such as the maize NAM where the RIL panels are all some founder crossed to a common parent).

Is that what you have? Or could you say more about the nature of these four families?

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] consensus map in Rqtl for NAM population
parts:
Got it, thanks.

For RIL, R/qtl ignores any heterozygous genotypes. So I'd code the genotypes in each of these crosses as A or B, with A = the common parent and B = the other parent, and then pool all of the sets as if it were a single panel of biparental RIL.

karl

Hello Karl,
Can I pull all four crosses together ? so that it can act as a single panel. If we will mix all four crosses does it affect the recombination  frequency? As in each cross the allelic variation will be different it may affect recombination frequency, If we will pull all crosses together, its my doubt. I need your opinin in this regard.

Thanks

Okay

On Dec 4, 2017 8:40 PM, "Karl Broman" <kbr...@gmail.com> wrote:
Got it, thanks.

For RIL, R/qtl ignores any heterozygous genotypes. So I'd code the genotypes in each of these crosses as A or B, with A = the common parent and B = the other parent, and then pool all of the sets as if it were a single panel of biparental RIL.

karl
